questions.question: How does the number of turns of wire in the coil affect the magnetic field of an electromagnet?
options: It has no effect on the magnetic field.
More turns of wire make the magnetic field stronger.
Fewer turns of wire make the magnetic field stronger.
More turns of wire make the magnetic field weaker.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the electrical current flowing through an electromagnet's coil and its magnetic field?
options: A higher current results in a stronger magnetic field.
A lower current results in a stronger magnetic field.
The current strength only affects the temperature, not the magnetic field.
The magnetic field remains completely constant regardless of current.

questions.question: Why must an electromagnet not be constructed from bare wire where adjacent loops touch each other?
options: The wire will melt instantly due to the high resistance.
The current will bypass the loops, and the electromagnet will not work.
The magnetic fields of adjacent loops will permanently cancel each other out.
The wire will become a permanent magnet and cannot be turned off.

questions.question: Why does inserting a soft iron core inside the coil of an electromagnet increase its overall strength?
options: The soft iron core conducts heat away to keep the coil cool.
The soft iron core reduces the overall electrical resistance of the wire.
The soft iron core becomes magnetised when the electric current is turned on.
The soft iron core permanently retains its magnetism even when the current is off.

questions.question: What occurs immediately around a straight wire when an electric current passes through it?
options: A magnetic field is generated around the wire.
The wire becomes statically charged and repels all metals.
A vacuum is created in the air surrounding the wire.
The wire permanently turns into a hard steel magnet.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary characteristic of an electromagnet that distinguishes it from a permanent magnet?
options: It only attracts non-metallic materials like plastic.
It can be turned on and off using an electric current.
It does not have a north or south pole.
Its magnetic field strength can never be altered.

questions.question: Which poles are found on every single magnet, regardless of its shape or size?
options: A positive pole and a negative pole.
An east-seeking pole and a west-seeking pole.
A north-seeking pole and a south-seeking pole.
An attracting pole and a neutral pole.

questions.question: If you bring the north-seeking pole of one bar magnet close to the north-seeking pole of another, what will happen?
options: The two poles will repel each other.
The two poles will attract each other.
Nothing will happen because they are the same pole.
The poles will temporarily demagnetise each other.

questions.question: How do unmagnetised magnetic materials, such as a piece of iron, behave near the poles of a magnet?
options: They are attracted to the north-seeking pole but repelled by the south-seeking pole.
They are repelled by both the north-seeking and south-seeking poles.
They are attracted to both the north-seeking and south-seeking poles.
They are only attracted to the poles if they are heated first.

questions.question: Which of the following groups contains only the three magnetic metal elements?
options: Iron, copper, and aluminium
Iron, cobalt, and nickel
Gold, silver, and copper
Cobalt, nickel, and zinc

questions.question: Why does the north-seeking pole of a freely suspended magnet point towards the Earth's geographic North Pole?
options: Due to the gravitational pull of the polar ice caps.
Because the Earth behaves as if it has a giant magnetic field.
Because of the rotation of the Earth on its axis.
Due to the high concentration of iron ore at the equator.

questions.question: What determines the direction in which a plotting compass needle points when placed near a bar magnet?
options: The temperature of the air around the magnet.
The needle lines up with the magnetic field of the magnet.
The needle points directly to the center of gravity of the magnet.
The needle points perpendicular to the closest magnetic field line.

questions.question: In which direction can a magnetic field line be traced outside a magnet?
options: From the south-seeking pole to the north-seeking pole.
From the center of the magnet outwards in all directions.
From the north-seeking pole to the south-seeking pole.
In circular loops that never connect to any poles.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key rule regarding how magnetic field lines are drawn?
options: They can cross each other where the magnetic field is strongest.
They are continuous and never cross over each other.
They start at the poles and end abruptly in space.
They only exist on the surface of the magnet and do not extend outwards.

questions.question: What is the role of the electromagnet inside a traditional electric bell?
options: It generates the sound waves directly through electric vibrations.
It attracts and moves the striker, causing it to hit the bell.
It heats up a bimetallic strip to trigger a physical hammer.
It acts as a battery to power the striker's movement.

questions.question: How does an electric motor cause its internal coil of wire to spin?
options: The heat generated by the current causes the coil to expand and rotate.
When there is a current in the coil, permanent magnets around it push it round.
Electrostatic repulsion from the casing pushes the wire around.
Gravity pulls the heavier side of the coil downward repeatedly.
